publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Education and Training for the Electronics Manufacturing Industry (Ref. No: 1997/084)
abstract: Summary form only given. This presentation outlines NEC Semiconductors (UK) Limited management's approach to continuous improvement through teamwork. NEC Scotland encourages each employee to work to their full potential allowing them to take on responsibility from an early stage in their career. It also stresses that employment security can only be gained from a successful company.

articleTitle: Future direction of large computer manufacturing companies
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Education and Training for the Electronics Manufacturing Industry (Ref. No: 1997/084)
abstract: Summary form only as given. This presentation deals with the possible future scenario for large-scale computer manufacturing companies for the Year 2000 and beyond, using experience of the computer industry particularly in Scotland and the European marketplace. It covers what is occurring in the PC industry generally, tracks industry trends and then quantifies what is likely to happen in terms of market growth and demand for the industry in the future. The author then looks into what manufacturing companies are doing to respond to the market; looking at manufacturing processes to prepare for the future. Finally, he discusses some visions of the future and on the likely outcome of this fiercely competitive industry.

articleTitle: Napier University and the electronics industry-progressing a strategic partnership
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Education and Training for the Electronics Manufacturing Industry (Ref. No: 1997/084)
abstract: The goal of this paper is to outline the strategic partnership that Napier University is developing with the electronics manufacturing industry, particularly the local industry in Scotland, which relate to education, training and research. The paper opens with two backcloths to this subject. First, a snapshot is presented in a broad overview of the shape, size, product range, growth prospects, and the human resource needs of electronics companies. Second, a description is given of the evolving style of Napier University to match and accommodate the ever changing education needs in today's world. The final section of this paper then summarizes the status of this strategic partnership.

articleTitle: Evaluation of skill requirements in contract electronics manufacture
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Education and Training for the Electronics Manufacturing Industry (Ref. No: 1997/084)
abstract: Within the contract electronic manufacturing industry the retention and development of the correct mix of people and skills is essential to achieve the vision of the organisation. The cost of acquiring and developing the necessary skills is an expensive business. The retention of employees is a major concern for companies particularly in areas of dense electronics manufacture. One of the methods which Design to Distribution (D2D) have begun to use to develop the appropriate mix of skills within the engineering section is modern apprenticeships. Modern apprenticeships are a new approach to work based training, developed by local training and enterprise councils (TECs) and employers, which enables the training to match the needs of the company. The trainees obtain a NVQ3 in an engineering discipline along with a BTEC award in electronics manufacturing. The apprenticeships enable the development of multi skilled, flexible and adaptable people with relevant technical expertise and knowledge. They should have supervisory, communication skills, the ability to work with others, solve problems and manage changes in information technology. This paper discusses the factors affecting the specification of a skills structure within a contract manufacturing organisation. It concentrates on the creation and retention of skills for printed circuit assembly and the use of modern apprenticeships as a means for satisfying company needs. The costs of training are assessed and the benefits and effectiveness of alternative approaches compared.

articleTitle: SQA provision for the electronics manufacturing industry
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Education and Training for the Electronics Manufacturing Industry (Ref. No: 1997/084)
abstract: The theme of this paper is the work that is ongoing within the Scottish Qualifications Authority (SQA) to meet the needs of the electronics manufacturing industry. It sets it in context alongside the wider national framework of engineering qualifications. A number of the initiatives will not fall into place until we are closer to the next millennium, notably in two areas: one is the implementation of 'Higher Still: Opportunity for All' to bridge the academic/vocational divide in the post-16 curriculum and the other is the completion of the framework of qualifications up to level V in the SVQ framework.

articleTitle: Starting an SME and the associated pitfalls [business management]
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Education and Training for the Electronics Manufacturing Industry (Ref. No: 1997/084)
abstract: This paper gives but a brief guide to avoiding some of the pitfalls of starting a small/medium-sized enterprise (SME). It should be remembered that being a director of a limited liability company carries a very heavy responsibility and that limited liability is no protection if directors are seen to have traded recklessly. Starting an SME is a risk and success will require long working hours, considerable planning and more than a little luck. However making a success of an SME is a very satisfying and worthwhile experience.

articleTitle: The impact of environmental issues on the UK electronics industry
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Education and Training for the Electronics Manufacturing Industry (Ref. No: 1997/084)
abstract: The need to adopt more environmentally responsible manufacturing practices in response to both public opinion and existing and forthcoming legislation is forcing industry to make major changes in the way it produces its products and offers its services. This is evident in the electronics industry and especially so in the printed circuit board (PCB) manufacturing sector. In this paper, the impact of environmental issues on the electronics industry in the United Kingdom is reviewed.

articleTitle: Scottish Advanced Manufacturing Centre: a case study of partnership
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Education and Training for the Electronics Manufacturing Industry (Ref. No: 1997/084)
abstract: The dynamic nature of process and technology evolution within the electronics industry requires equivalent changes within the academic sector for training and research. Career and vocational training which supports industry trends must maintain that workforce infrastructure and provide opportunities for career development and growth. The Scottish Advanced Manufacturing Centre (SAMC) has evolved as a research and education resource for the electronics industry. This Centre, located in the heart of Scotland's Silicon Glen, provides a partnership between education and industrial institutions which focuses on sector needs, strategic aims and technology evolution. In addition, SAMC facilitates the strategic collaboration between industry and academia to focus on supply, technology and processes which will maintain market leadership. SAMC has evolved from a close relationship between Napier University's Scottish Electronics Manufacturing Centre and West Lothian College. This paper provides an overview of the development of SAMC as a strategic resource to the electronics industry.

articleTitle: Training of tomorrow's engineers for the electronics manufacturing industry
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Education and Training for the Electronics Manufacturing Industry (Ref. No: 1997/084)
abstract: The training requirements of undergraduate electronic engineering students is discussed relative to the needs of manufacturing. Course structure for fourth year M.Eng. students is examined and its relationship to future employment determined. The techniques seen in electronics assembly are contrasted using case studies and industrial visits.

articleTitle: Electronics to optoelectronics-opportunities for the 21st Century
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Education and Training for the Electronics Manufacturing Industry (Ref. No: 1997/084)
abstract: The author argues that optoelectronics offers a wide range of opportunities and challenges and must be an integral part of the educational curriculum and training schemes, post-graduation, to ensure competence in the field. These are major issues for the large number of electrical engineers who are and will be involved in the future.

articleTitle: Defect data system in PCB and electronics manufacturing
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Education and Training for the Electronics Manufacturing Industry (Ref. No: 1997/084)
abstract: In order to ensure all products are manufactured to approved quality standards, and are in complete conformance with the relevant specifications, it is essential to monitor process control. To enable the monitoring and analysis of process control in the manufacture of PCBs and electronic assemblies in a more timely and efficient manner, the authors have introduced a new defect data system. The new system is PC-based, using a bar code scanner enabling rapid defect data collection, which replaced the previous paper system. The purpose of collecting defect data is to ensure that those responsible for an activity are informed if something has gone wrong, in order that corrective and preventive action can be taken.
